memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But my covenant I will establish with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear to you by this time next year." When he had finished speaking with Abraham, God went up from him. - Gen 17:21-22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God sets a date. "By this time next year" Sarah would bear Isaac. After decades of waiting, after so many years of vague future promise, God now gives a specific appointment. The fulfilment is no longer "someday" - it is one year away. God's promises, so long delayed, do come due at last.

There is such encouragement in this precision. God had not forgotten. He had not been vague or evasive. In His perfect timing, He names the very season when the impossible would become real. The waiting had an end, and God knew exactly when it would come.

We often live in the long stretch of "someday," wondering if God's promises will ever arrive. Genesis 17 reminds us that God keeps appointments. His timing may be far slower than ours, but it is never late. What He has promised, He will bring to pass at exactly the right moment.

Notice the quiet close: "God went up from him." The encounter ends; God withdraws His visible presence. But the promise remains, ticking down toward its fulfilment. Even when God seems to have gone up and away, His word is still at work. "The vision... will certainly come and will not delay" (Hab 2:3). Whatever you are waiting for, God keeps His appointments. Trust His perfect timing.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you stuck in the long stretch of "someday," waiting on God?
- Can you trust that God keeps His appointments in His perfect timing?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that You keep Your appointments and Your timing is never late. In my long seasons of waiting, help me trust that Your promises will come due at exactly the right moment. I rest in Your perfect timing.
Amen.
